title: Desolace
body: Desolace is a grey and broken land southwest of the Stonetalon Mountains, a waste of bare rock, bleached bones and brackish yellow pools beneath a stormy sky. Only the western shore, where the Veiled Sea breaks on the Sar'theris Strand, keeps any green. This is the ancestral home of the centaur, whose holy ground of Maraudon lies hidden deep in the Valley of Spears. Their clans, the Kolkar, Gelkis, Magram and Maraudine, now fight one another across the plains, and outsiders dread the day they might unite. They are not the only danger. The night elves who once lived here are long gone, the Burning Blade holds Thunder Axe Fortress, demons gather at Mannoroc Coven, Hatefury satyrs haunt Sargeron and naga prowl the coast. The Alliance keeps watch from Nijel's Point in the northern mountains, while the Horde holds Ghost Walker Post above the Kodo Graveyard and the troll fishing village of Shadowprey.

title: Nijel's Point
body: Hidden in the mountains of northern Desolace, just east of the way in from Stonetalon, Nijel's Point is a small Alliance camp, easily missed. No one there seems to know who Nijel was. Soldiers of Stormwind guard it under Captain Pentigast, who studies how to break the warring centaur clans, while Corporal Melkins pays for every centaur ear brought in. Night elves keep the inn and the hippogryph roost, and Vahlarriel Demonslayer has come from Darnassus to find two missing nobles. Kreldig Ungor of Reclaimers Inc. hunts down lost property for paying clients, Brother Anton preaches the cause of the Scarlet Crusade, and the keeper Marandis and his sisters of the Cenarion Circle have business with Maraudon.

title: Sargeron
body: In the northeastern corner of Desolace stand the ruins of a night elf city that has lain broken since the War of the Ancients, its true name forgotten. The Hatefury satyrs who infest it call it Sargeron, after their dark master Sargeras. Rogues, tricksters, betrayers, felsworn, hellcallers and shadowstalkers prowl the fallen streets as allies of the Burning Blade. Maurin Bonesplitter of Ghost Walker Post has a use for a shadowstalker's scalp in his spellwork. Kreldig Ungor of Nijel's Point doubts the tale that the satyr are tied to the night elves, blaming it on the one elf who brought them into the war a few years back.

title: Thunder Axe Fortress
body: Thunder Axe Fortress rises in northern Desolace, just south of the ruins of Tethris Aran, and belongs to the Burning Blade, orcs who have given their loyalty to demons. From its stronghold, barracks and watchtowers the cult's augurs, adepts, reavers, felsworn and shadowmages practice their dark craft. Within lies a red crystal sealing the Demon Box, which holds the Hand of Iruxos the cult uses to open portals at Mannoroc Coven, and atop one watchtower a Burning Blade seer studies the Sceptre of Light, taken from the naga. Not everyone within the walls belongs to the cult. Among the fires of the stronghold stands a night elf woman whom the orcs around her leave be.

title: Ethel Rethor
body: On the northwestern coast the ruins of Ethel Rethor lie mostly beneath the waves, a drowned night elf city whose only standing remnant is a lone tower reached by a small bridge. From it the Argent Dawn mage Azore Aldamort watches both the Slitherblade naga who haunt the shallows and the Burning Blade to the east. Nearby lies the chest of the Stormwind mage Karnitol, who abandoned it when sea giants fell upon his ship offshore and saved himself and his servants by magic, leaving it behind for whoever might come looking.

title: Ranazjar Isle
body: On Ranazjar Isle, a small rocky island off the northwestern coast, Slitherblade sea witches, tidehunters, myrmidons and oracles gather about a great serpent statue. Close by, sunken night elf ruins on the sea floor serve the Slitherblade as a home. The Argent Dawn knows that a gem set in the statue's hand will call forth the protector of the Book of the Ancients, which holds secrets the naga have kept for centuries. Drulzegar Skraghook's fishing crew was slaughtered by naga near the isle, and when Rackmore's ship was attacked by sea creatures on its way to Feathermoon Stronghold, he hid his treasure here in a chest that needs two keys, one silver and one gold.

title: Sar'theris Strand
body: The Sar'theris Strand runs along the western coast, the one stretch of Desolace that still knows sun and grass. Slitherblade naga come ashore from their reefs, drysnap crawlers scuttle in the surf, and Deepstrider giants wade the shallows, the kind of sea giants that drove a Stormwind mage from his ship off the northern shore. A wrecked ship lies off the coast north of Shadowprey Village, where soft-shelled clams prized by troll fishermen as bait litter the sea bed, and waterlogged footlockers turn up among the rocks. Near Shadowprey, the dryad Selendra and her sisters have come down from Stonetalon on a mission they cannot finish alone, and seek mortals strong enough to help.

title: Kormek's Hut
body: Kormek's Hut is a lonely shack on the barren flats of north-central Desolace, southeast of Thunder Axe Fortress, and of Kormek himself there is no sign. The goblin Bibbly F'utzbuckle has taken over its pen, sure that he is sitting on a goldmine. Kodo bones from the graveyard to the south, he claims, go into furniture, musical instruments and even blasting powder, and a caravan collects them to sell at Shadowprey Village. That caravan, the Gizelton brothers' kodo train, halts on the road outside. Inside waits a stranger guest, Willow of the Twilight's Hammer, who pays for crystal carvings from the caverns of Maraudon, relics of the old gods whose powers, Willow says, have been too long at rest.

title: Kolkar Village
body: The Kolkar hold the eastern reaches of Desolace from a village northeast of Ghost Walker Post, beneath the mountains. Desolace is their homeland, and from it their warbands have spread into the Barrens. The Horde holds that as long as the clan stays strong here it will always be a threat. Battle lords, destroyers, maulers, windchasers and scouts crowd the camp under Khan Dez'hepah. The rival clans scorn them: the Gelkis say the Kolkar would not know true magic if it bit them, and the Magram laugh as they kill them. Travelers fear them all the same. When the Gizelton caravan hears the Kolkar war drums, it stops dead on the road and waits for a bodyguard.

title: Scrabblescrew's Camp
body: Smeed Scrabblescrew's camp sits beside the road through central Desolace, a goblin's stake in the one caravan bold enough to brave these lands. Smeed claims to have learned how to rejuvenate and control aged and dying kodo with a device of his own, the kodo kombobulator, which jolts the beasts into tame pack animals. He supplies them to Cork and Rigger Gizelton, whose caravan pays his bills, and he pays the bodyguards who see it safely through, though he grumbles at every coin. Smeed fancies himself a far better businessman than Bibbly F'utzbuckle of Kormek's Hut, and can hardly wait to see the look on his rival's green face when word of his success gets around.

title: Ghost Walker Post
body: Ghost Walker Post is a tauren outpost in central Desolace, north of the great Kodo Graveyard, reached by the road south from the Charred Vale. From here the Horde deals with the centaur clans and the Burning Blade. The tauren Gurda Wildmane seeks an alliance with one of the clans, while Felgur Twocuts gathers intelligence on them. Orgrimmar sent its own envoys, the orc swordsman Takata Steelblade and the Forsaken warlock Maurin Bonesplitter, to root out the demons, at the word of Keldran. Ghost Walker braves keep watch, Nataka Longhorn longs for fried fish from Shadowprey, and Narv Hidecrafter swears the strongest hides come from kodo that have laid themselves to rest in this wasteland.

title: Kodo Graveyard
body: South of Ghost Walker Post spreads the Kodo Graveyard, a field of enormous skeletons where kodo come to lay themselves to rest. Aged, dying and ancient kodo wander slowly among the bones of their kin, and carrion horrors haunt the field. Many of the bones seem to have belonged to beasts far larger than any kodo alive today, and grave moss grows thick in their shadow. Where death gathers, so do goblins. Bibbly F'utzbuckle of Kormek's Hut pays for every bone carried out of here, and Hornizz Brimbuzzle keeps a camp at the graveyard's edge, forever waiting on his restless sister Melizza and the next deal, even one made of ghosts.

title: Mannoroc Coven
body: Named for the pit lord Mannoroth, Mannoroc Coven lies south of Ghost Walker Post among old night elf ruins, a land already dead that the demons have blasted further with fel magic. Burning Blade summoners opened portals here, and through them the Legion came: lesser infernals, doomwarders, felhounds that hunt mages, and succubi called nether maidens, sisters and sorceresses. Their master is the demon lord Azrethoc, and the orc warlock Jugkar Grim'rod serves at his side. Even the Gizelton caravan's kodo shy at the coven. At its southern edge an exiled centaur, the Pariah, nurses his dream of a single great tribe.

title: Shadowbreak Ravine
body: Hidden in the mountains southeast of Magram Village, Shadowbreak Ravine is a secret enclave of the Burning Blade, far from the eyes of travelers on the road. Summoners and invokers of the cult practice their arts here, kin to those who call demons into Mannoroc Coven, and ley hunters, felhounds that feed on magic, prowl among them. The cultists keep something else in the ravine as well: captured stallions, kept beside dark steeds that bear the cult's name, the Burning Blade nightmares. What the cultists mean to do with them they do not say.

title: Magram Village
body: The Magram centaur hold the southeast of Desolace, their camps spread out at the foot of the eastern mountains. They are a clan that respects only strength. Wranglers, stormers, marauders, maulers and windchasers run with their bonepaws, and sacks of dried meat are stored so the clan can fight longer between hunts. Khan Jehn rules them, and the Gelkis would like nothing better than his head. On the outskirts, under the eyes of his bodyguards, waits Warug, the clan's spokesman, who will hear any outsider strong enough to slay the Gelkis. To the Magram, the Gelkis faith in their mother Theradras is nothing but weakness, and they mean to prove it.

title: Valley of Bones
body: At the southern edge of Desolace lies the Valley of Bones, a crag where the vast skeletons of two Dead Goliaths have collapsed against the cliffs, their origin unknown. Undead ravagers stalk its floor, outcast necromancers move among them, and the valley is haunted by the ghosts of the Magram. It draws outsiders all the same. Brother Anton of the Scarlet Crusade sends would-be recruits here to destroy the ravagers as proof of their resolve, and the goblin Hornizz Brimbuzzle hands out crates of ghost magnets to lure the spirits between the two great skeletons, sure that the Magram will pay a fortune for captured ghost-o-plasm, if only he can convince them what it is.

title: Gelkis Village
body: The Gelkis centaur dwell in the far southwest of Desolace, their village ringing a ravine crossed by bridges beside the main road south. Theirs is the clan of the earth. Their shamans call on Theradras, whom they hold to be the mother of the centaur, and trust that she protects them. In the cave of Bolgan's Hole, where Khan Shaka keeps his seat, they hoard the blue crystals called tears of Theradras. The shaman Uthek the Wise waits in a tent on the outskirts for strangers willing to spill Magram blood. The Gelkis and the Magram are brother clans and mortal enemies, set apart by faith in the earth against faith in strength.

title: Valley of Spears
body: The Valley of Spears in western Desolace belongs to the Maraudine, the clan that guards Maraudon, holy ground where only spirits and the most sacred priests may tread. Maraudine scouts, stormers and priests roam its canyons, and ghostly raiders ride among them. A war horn stands atop a high bluff, and its call brings the clan's warriors and at last Khan Hratha himself. In the caves at the valley's end the dryad Cavindra begs for help for her cursed brother and sisters, and the Nameless Prophet, one of the oldest of all the tribes, communes with the spirits of the ancestors. The goblin Melizza Brimbuzzle came here to trade and ended up in a cage.

title: Shadowprey Village
body: Shadowprey Village is a Darkspear troll fishing village on the western coast of Desolace, its docks reaching into the sea, and its catch is wanted inland at Ghost Walker Post. Tauren keep the inn and the wind riders. Fishermen of every temper work the docks: Jinar'Zillen pays others to empty his shellfish traps, Mai'Lahii would rather fish than sell tackle, and Drulzegar Skraghook lives only for revenge on the naga who killed his crew. Taiga Wisemane fights the demons of Mannoroc Coven, Vark Battlescar works to heal the corruption of Maraudon, and the tauren Roon Wildmane remembers the days he hunted with the dwarf Hemet Nesingwary.

title: Warug
body: Warug speaks for the Magram clan, on the edge of Magram Village, his bodyguards close at hand. He respects strength and nothing else, and will not speak with anyone who has not slain many Gelkis. For those who have, he has work: smash the tears of Theradras the Gelkis hoard, bring him the head of Khan Shaka so he can stare at it and laugh, and break the Maraudine. He laughs when he kills, so the enemy can see he is weak. Yet Warug has a childish streak. Long ago he killed a gnome who came with a cart of strange moving things, and he still wants a new wooden target dummy to replace the one he broke.

title: Uthek the Wise
body: Uthek the Wise is a shaman of the Gelkis who keeps a tent on the outskirts of their village and listens to what the earth tells her. To strangers whose hands are wet with Magram blood she gives tasks and counsel: the Magram hoard meat to fight longer, the Kolkar know nothing of true magic, and the earth has whispered to her of a red crystal called draenethyst, new to this world, from a place where mountains fly and demons rule. For a shard of it she would send an ally as far as the Swamp of Sorrows. Earth magic, Uthek says, is stronger than any khan's might, and one day the Gelkis will rule.

title: Captain Pentigast
body: Captain Pentigast commands the Stormwind soldiers who guard Nijel's Point. He sees Desolace as a land at war, and fears that whichever centaur clan wins will spill out and threaten the Alliance's strongholds. His answer is cold reckoning. The clans fight among themselves, and if they ever joined into one force they would be unstoppable, so the Alliance must press its advantage: side with the Gelkis or the Magram, earn their favor by killing their rivals, and learn from them how to beat all the centaurs. His corporal, Melkins, holds to a simpler policy, paying for centaur ears in the belief that each one brings the war a step closer to its end.

He is a soldier first, bound to his post by duty to the Warchief and by the honor of his clan. The fight wears on him. The demons only seem to multiply, his hope of returning to the Warchief dwindles, and at times he wishes the centaur were his only foes.

His creed is war with the Scourge, an evil that corrupts the people and infects the land. Those who would join must first prove themselves against the undead ravagers of the Valley of Bones. The worthy he sends back across the sea with a letter of commendation for Raleigh the Devout in Southshore, who will escort them to the Crusade's Scarlet Monastery, for the true threat of the plague, he insists, lies in Lordaeron.

title: The Centaur Pariah

The tribes fight one another for scraps left by vultures and lands infested by the Legion, when their heritage is as noble as any night elf's or orc's. His dream is one great tribe, and exile has not shaken his belief in it. For his destiny to be complete he needs an outsider of no tribe, one willing to enter the holy halls of Maraudon, a tomb only the most devout of his people may enter.

title: The Kolkar of Desolace
body: From his bunkers in the Barrens, Regthar Deathgate recruits agents for a mission against the centaur of Desolace, a land torn by war, for as long as the Kolkar stay strong in their homeland they will threaten the plains. His volunteers go to Felgur Twocuts at Ghost Walker Post, who has been gathering intelligence on the clans and warns that the struggle will be long. Many clans wander the dry plains, fighting and dying against each other, and that is a mercy, for united they would be a fierce foe. The Horde must act before they unite, and Felgur means to start with the Kolkar leader, Khan Dez'hepah, in his village to the northeast. At the same post Gurda Wildmane has a subtler plan: ally with one clan and learn from it how to defeat them all.

body: Captain Pentigast at Nijel's Point and Gurda Wildmane at Ghost Walker Post reach the same conclusion: the way to beat the centaur is through their hatred of one another. United, the clans would be unstoppable; divided, they can be played against one another, and whoever wins the friendship of one may learn from it the way to beat them all. One who slays enough Magram may win a hearing with Uthek the Wise of the Gelkis, while one who slays Gelkis may stand before Warug of the Magram. Neither clan gives its trust freely. Each sets its new friends task after task written in the blood of its rivals, and Alliance champions are sent against the Kolkar as well.

parts.body: The Malem wagon was found wrecked by spells and weapons, in a fight that had been swift and one-sided, with no blood and no bodies. A pendant lay in the wreckage, and footprints led south toward a fort where smoke rose from a kept fire. Vahlarriel was furious, for the two had been warned. From what the locals said, the fortress was infested with the Burning Blade, orcs dedicated to demon causes, who slay spies on sight.

parts.body: Vahlarriel's superiors in Darnassus cared most that Dalinda come home safe; Tyranis was to be gauged first. Dalinda was found a prisoner within the fortress, brought there with her brother by the Burning Blade and sure she would be sacrificed. Coming to Desolace had been a mistake, she said: Tyranis had begun to crave knowledge of all things arcane, against the wishes of their people, and had made the journey even after hearing of the demons.
sources: quest 1438 reward text
quest 1439 description (offered next: will not leave until his fate is known)

parts.body: She would not leave until his fate was known, and it was the fate she had dreaded. Tyranis had sought the cult's secrets and counted himself among their kind, and he died at her rescuers' hands, as he surely would have at her own people's. Dalinda called it necessary, and asked forgiveness if her thanks did not sound sincere.
sources: quest 1439 completion and reward text

parts.body: Only then did Dalinda flee the fortress. Partway out she sent her escort back to finish off the cultists and went on alone, and she reached Nijel's Point under her own power. Vahlarriel was glad of it, but grieved that both had not come back. The shame of her brother's choices is Dalinda's to carry home to Darnassus.

title: The Corrupter
body: Among the Burning Blade's cultists some carry a strip of flayed demon skin, rotten-smelling and strangely supple for something that looks so dry and fragile. Red markings in some unknown language cover one side, and at the bottom sits a clear symbol that seems to be a signature of some kind. Such a thing belongs before Maurin Bonesplitter at Ghost Walker Post, a Forsaken warlock who knows the cult's ways and scorns them. If anyone in Desolace can tell what the markings say, and whose mark is set beneath them, it is he.

To find him Maurin first needed the scalp of a Hatefury shadowstalker from the ruins of Sargeron, to break any wards the demon held against scrying.

parts.body: With the scalp in hand and an oracle crystal from the Slitherblade naga to focus the spell, Maurin called Azrethoc by his true name, and the demon lord's image appeared. The creature was far more dangerous than Maurin had expected. Rather than face it alone he sent word to Takata Steelblade, the swordsman beside him, whose honor demanded he be told, with a warning not to press him too hard.

Lord Azrethoc and his orc warlock servant Jugkar Grim'rod were slain at Mannoroc Coven, and Takata dared to hope that the Horde might one day have a place it could safely call home again.

title: The Hand of Iruxos
body: Taiga Wisemane of Shadowprey Village has learned that the Burning Blade possesses a Demon Box holding the Hand of Iruxos, the relic the cult uses to open demonic portals at Mannoroc Coven and let a tide of demons into the world. The box lies sealed within a red crystal at Thunder Axe Fortress, the cult's stronghold in the north, and Taiga provides a demon pick to break it free. The tide must be stopped, and Taiga wants the box carried back to Shadowprey, pick and all, so that what lies inside can be turned to that end.

parts.body: The Hand was a gruesome sight, but Taiga turned the cult's own tool against it: carried into Mannoroc Coven, it could banish the portals. Each portal sent forth a guardian when the Hand was set against it, but six were banished and the flood of demons was stemmed. The effort had helped greatly in the fight against the demon threat, Taiga declared, and all of Azeroth was safer because of it.

title: The Karnitol Shipwreck
body: Reclaimers Inc., the Ironforge firm that finds what people have lost for the right price, sent the dwarf Kreldig Ungor to Nijel's Point with a list of jobs. The first is for Karnitol, a mage and noble of Stormwind, whose ship was attacked by sea giants off the northwest coast. He tried to bring a valuable chest ashore, then abandoned it and teleported himself and his servants to safety, and now he wants it found. The other is a shopping list for Leftwitch, a gnome mage of Kharanos, beginning with horns and claws from the Hatefury satyr. Roetten in Ironforge thinks it easy coin, though Kreldig is short-handed as it is.

parts.body: Kreldig blamed the Slitherblade naga, who make their home in sunken night elf ruins near Ranazjar Isle, and Karnitol's satchel turned up among their tidehunters and sea witches. Those blasted naga, Kreldig grumbled: he would rather spend his life at war with the Horde than go up against their kind.

parts.body: Leftwitch's list grew stranger as it went: scorpashi venom, the hide of aged kodo and no other, and at last felhound brains, nether wings and doomwarder blood from the demons of Mannoroc Coven. Kreldig had not even known there were demons in Desolace, a land he thought the centaur owned once the night elves left, and he wondered how they came to be there.

title: The Gizelton Caravan
body: The goblin brothers Cork and Rigger Gizelton run the only caravan brave enough to cross Desolace, a kodo train hauling their wares between a stop outside Kormek's Hut in the north and another on the southern road east of Shadowprey Village. At each stop a selling machine opens for business, Cork's Vendor-Tron 1000 and Rigger's Super-Seller 680, and Cork, his brother says, is sure his own will sell more. The road between is perilous. Near the Kolkar village the centaur war drums make the brothers halt until someone will guard them past, and farther south, where the demons of Mannoroc Coven usually ignore them, something has spooked the kodo. Bodyguards collect their pay from the brothers' partner Smeed Scrabblescrew, who supplies the kodo.

If he were a bit taller, he mused, he would ride kodo-back with the biggest gun he could carry and show the centaur a thing or two himself.

parts.body: The caravan came safely through Mannoroc Coven, and Smeed wiped his brow and thanked the goddess of greed, for if it ever disappeared he would be ruined. He still doubts the sense of paying so much to guard it, since Cork and Rigger make only one gold piece a week, but as long as they keep buying his kodo he cares little how they run their business.

title: The Corruption of Maraudon
body: At the end of the Valley of Spears lies Maraudon, holy ground of the centaur and the root of their story. Keeper Marandis at Nijel's Point and Selendra near Shadowprey have come down from Stonetalon with their sisters on a mission for the Cenarion Circle, to lay to rest a sorrow from ages past, and they seek allies strong enough to see it done. The caverns are fouled besides: the satyr Lord Vyletongue poisoned them and made Noxxion as a living symbol of his corruption. Talendria and Vark Battlescar seek to heal the vines he twisted, and Cavindra pleads for her brother Celebras, wandering cursed within, his scepter stolen in two pieces.

parts.body: The sorrow is the centaur's own beginning. Ages ago Zaetar, first son of Cenarius, came together with Princess Theradras, an elemental force of earth somehow kin to the Old Gods, and their offspring became the centaur. The children repaid their father by killing him, and his remains lie in Maraudon still. The Circle seeks those strong enough to slay Theradras, so that Zaetar's remains can be recovered and carried back to Stonetalon.
sources: quests 7064, 7065 descriptions (Zaetar, Theradras, the centaur killed their father; slay Theradras, recover the remains, return to Stonetalon)

parts.body: Purified water from the orange crystal pool was poured on the Vylestem vines, and the corrupted scions Vyletongue sent up out of them were cut down. Some of the corruption he spread through Maraudon was healed and the plants could grow again, though much remains to be done.
sources: quests 7029, 7041 descriptions, objectives and reward texts

parts.body: Both pieces of the Scepter of Celebras, the Celebrian Rod and the Celebrian Diamond, were taken back from Vyletongue and Noxxion, and Celebras woke as if from a nightmare that seemed it would never end. With the two parts of his scepter recovered, he has hope that Maraudon may one day be rid of the corruption.
sources: quest 7044 description, objectives, completion and reward text (Celebras the Redeemed 13716 ends it)

parts.body: Princess Theradras was slain in the depths of Maraudon. Zaetar, brother to Remulos, had brought many pains to the world, Selendra said, and in the end they caused his death. It was the hardest of the tasks the dryads had come for, and Selendra rewarded her slayers with tokens of her people, as she had been given leave to do. Zaetar's remains are not yet settled: on that, Selendra means to seek the wisdom of Keeper Marandis.

parts.body: Princess Theradras was slain in the depths of Maraudon. Zaetar, brother to Remulos, had brought many pains to the world and his own death with them, and there is a lesson in that, Marandis said. His remains did not come back with her slayers, and though it concerns him, Keeper Marandis will not question the will of Cenarius' first born. Perhaps now, he hopes, the will of the centaur will break and their thirst for blood will lessen.
